title: Lost posters, stolen material and Ralph Cooper's revue
summary: Faded write-ups, crooked booking agents, and the Ralph Cooper revue; Albert was leader, trumpeter, agent and father to the band.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Managers, bookers and the business of getting work

blocks.x: Oh, when the band was built on posters and then advertisements in the newspapers and stuff like that. I think we talked about this before. Do you have any of those posters or ads to show how to build?

I sure wish I did. Danny Balka asked me that question here. Yeah. And, of course, here's what happens. When you're young, you're going great, you don't think of what's gonna happen in the future. Mm-hmm. I should have said, well I have quite a number of old write-ups that have faded that you barely can read.
You ought to get those Xerox. That's the thing. Take them down.

I don't believe you could even Xerox and there's so much on it that, maybe I might send you one of these books and you can pick out what you think could be Xerox. You can pick out these Xerox at your convenience and at your time.
Yeah, I might find somebody who could do it in some sort of special way.

Maybe so. But, I have a few of them. And then too, a lot of this stuff was stolen from me. The Booking Age, it's like Al Travis, the biggest crook in the world. Then comes Rabinowitz, another Jewish Booking Age. And this guy, Chauncey Hallin. These guys take my material and when they jump the gun, I never see them on my material and all that's gone. Which was a big loss to me. Pictures, stories, and things like that.
Well, I guess sometimes you'd get top billing and sometimes you wouldn't. Well, yeah. It was very.

Top billing and most of the time in the cities but on the stages might have been a review. So, you're just another part of the review. So, for instance, this is Ralph Cooper's review. Mm-hmm. Featuring Don Albert's Big Bang. Who was Ralph Cooper? Ralph Cooper was a producer in New York. Mm-hmm. He was just like Larry Steele and those guys who don't know anything about him. I only heard their name. But they were producers. He produced the show at the Fowlers in Brooklyn. That's where Ella and all these other upcoming stars. We had a big production. Mm-hmm. And Glens Falls, New York. We had Billy Holiday up in Glens Falls, New York. And the buildings, everyone would, Ralph Cooper would be the headliner. Yeah. So, so, so, so, so.
Yeah, well, that's more honest than the way they do things now sometimes. I don't know.
Well, today, if you don't give a man Todd Billing, he might walk out on you.

Yeah. Well, I mean, sometimes you need to know who the producer of a show is. Because they, guys, they had certain reputations. Right. And some producers had integrity and some of them didn't. Some guys, you know, it seemed to me that they're good producers. They deserve a lot of credit. Right. People don't realize that. Just like a lot of people don't think a band leader does anything. They don't know what he does after the show is open, before it goes on.
They don't know what he does when the others are sleeping. Yeah. And in my case, I had to do the leader, trumpet player, booking agent, and father and mother to the band. Mm-hmm.
Yeah, you had to do everything.
